g.text: STUDENT IDENTITY 2.1 — a second chain off the SAME root
THE HASH CHAIN — one function, every log-producing path goes through it
VERIFICATION — server or browser, years later
ONE delegation hop, not two: the institution
key lives on a server and mints on demand,
which is what the offline course key cannot do
signs root_sig. The root key signs
never a credential, never a log

g.title: rkpub
g.text: server and in the browser build
server-side and in the browser build.

g.title: ckpriv
g.text: never on a server or in git

g.title: amf
g.text: scope · policy ← all of it covered by sig

g.title: sbind
g.text: A keypair, NOT a bearer token: a uuid is copyable and
repudiable, a signature is not — and the server holds
only PUBLIC keys, so a breach forges nobody

g.title: bind
g.text: (2) session privkey AEAD-wrapped under a key
HKDF-derived from that same manifest sig

g.title: rseal
g.text: file, rewritten at start, after checkpoints (min 60 s apart,
late ones deferred), ~1 s after a save, and at dispose. Its digests commit to a PREFIX — except the
dispose-time roll, which carries final: true inside the
signed payload and commits to the WHOLE file.
each session signs its OWN seal,
so no key can vouch for another

g.title: scred
g.text: Issued by the SERVER from /enroll — no course,
no semester, and NO roster row required

g.title: e0
g.text: course_cert) · identity · host, and the three
never a git author, never the upload filename.
Absent is the ORDINARY case and is blameless.

g.title: pol
g.text: capture policy — signed, so a professor can
turn capture DOWN and a student cannot turn it OFF
the schema has no key that could disable it.
the EFFECTIVE policy rides into the bundle,
so the analyzer can tell 'not recorded by
deferred) and ~1 s after a save —

g.title: push
g.text: No seal step ever runs, so the archived
log routinely runs past its own last seal.
fans the repo out per scope
